name: Ötzi Dorf
kurzbeschreibung: The Ötzi Village in Umhausen is an archaeological open-air park depicting everyday life, housing, and survival during the Neolithic era of the Iceman.
preis: Adults approx. €12.00, children (6–15 yrs) €6.50, combined tickets with birds of prey park available
oeffnungszeiten: Early May to late October daily 09:30–17:30 (closing at 17:00 in October)
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned Ötzi Village (Ötzi-Dorf) in Umhausen in the central Ötztal is an archaeological open-air park that vividly illustrates everyday living, crafts, and prehistoric alpine survival during the Neolithic Age. Inspired by the sensational 1991 discovery of „Ötzi the Iceman“—the 5,300-year-old glacier mummy found on the nearby Tisenjoch ridge—the park features an authentically reconstructed prehistoric settlement. Sprawling across scenic alpine terrain, the park provides captivating educational insights into Neolithic architecture, hunting strategies, primitive agriculture, and clothing, attracting tens of thousands of visitors each season.

Route & Requirements

Along an expansive looped trail, visitors explore true-to-scale reconstructions of Neolithic timber huts, workshops, hunting shelters, bread ovens, and grain storage granaries. Informative interpretive panels, display vitrines, and live demonstrations reveal how flint tools were knapped, animal skins sewn into garments, and prehistoric cereals ground into flour. Children especially adore the enclosures housing ancient domestic animal breeds, including woolly Mangalitza pigs, rare Soay sheep, and native wild trout in the stream. The entire open-air grounds feature compacted gravel paths navigable with all-terrain prams. Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate outdoor apparel are advised.

Visit & Arrival

The open-air village is open daily from early May to late October, operating from 09:30 to 17:30 (closing at 17:00 in October). Standard admission for adults is approx. €12.00, children €6.50; discounted combined tickets including the adjacent Birds of Prey Park are very popular. By public transit: take the train to Ötztal Bahnhof and transfer to the comfortable Ötztaler bus line to Umhausen Feuerwehr, followed by a pleasant 15-minute walk along the brook. Motorists take the A12 motorway to the Ötztal exit, follow the B186 federal road into Umhausen, and park at the Stuibenfall car park.

Tips

Directly adjacent to the open-air park is the Birds of Prey Park Umhausen, presenting breathtaking daily flight demonstrations with eagles, falcons, and owls against alpine peaks. Combine your excursion with a scenic hike to the nearby Stuibenfall, Tyrol's highest waterfall with an exhilarating drop of 159 meters, accessible via suspended walkways and lookout platforms. An on-site rustic bistro offers refreshments and snacks.
